inspected: official/public Phase-2 rules and FlopScope documentation

confirmed_violations.finding: math.sqrt executes output-affecting estimator numerical work in CPython outside FlopScope. Official Phase-2 summary limits stdlib math to control/bookkeeping/loading, says meaningful unmetered computation is a breach, and provides billed fnp.sqrt.

confirmed_unmetered_but_standalone_eligi.finding: _statics(n) performs Python scalar arithmetic/divisions inside predict to derive output-affecting coefficients.
1.0 / math.sqrt(...) is a Python scalar division before the result is multiplied into a FlopScope array.
Python float conversions/coefficient arithmetic prepare scalar factors outside the array meter.

findings.ambiguity_basis: FlopScope v0.12.1 README itself demonstrates fnp.sqrt(2 / width), leaving shape-derived Python scalar division outside the metered sqrt. Official materials do not define a blanket de-minimis/scalar-arithmetic eligibility boundary. These scalar cases are therefore not independently promoted to confirmed violations.
confirmed_non_violations: No numpy/scipy/BLAS/FFI/concurrency/torch/jax import in the grader import path.
No float(fnp...), bool(fnp...), or int(fnp...) scalar materialization found.
Operators on fnp arrays and fnp sum/mean/sqrt/power/clip/einsum/linalg.qr remain on documented metered paths.
R244 source uses neither fnp.full nor fnp.full_like; the official starter-kit states that non-scalar full/full_like is the only 0.12.1 pricing change relative to the live 0.12.0 grader meter.
unknowns: Whether an external packaging/static scanner rejects the local_engine import under the unreachable __main__ guard.
The official materials do not explicitly define when small shape-derived Python scalar arithmetic crosses the 'meaningful computation' threshold.

workflow_provenance.version_assessment: Starter-kit pyproject explicitly documents the one-patch lead and says only non-scalar full/full_like pricing changes in flopscope 0.12.1. R244 uses neither, so that known patch-level pricing difference does not apply.

next_step: Do not modify or rerun R244. For any future distinct candidate, preregister a source-level compliance gate requiring output-affecting sqrt/transcendental numerical work in predict to use FlopScope (e.g. fnp.sqrt), and obtain organizer clarification before relying on nontrivial free Python-scalar arithmetic.
